description.main: Catalogue of the 2014 exhibition at Museo Jumex, Mexico City, the first comprehensive showing of Cy Twombly's work in Latin America. It reproduces 57 works from the early 1950s to the Camino Real paintings of 2011, with an essay by Philip Larratt-Smith.
description.extended:
The catalogue of the first comprehensive exhibition of Cy Twombly's work in Latin America, held at Museo Jumex in Mexico City from June 5 to October 12, 2014.

Curated by Julie Sylvester and Philip Larratt-Smith and edited by Sylvester, the book reproduces 57 works on paper, paintings, and sculptures, with double-page details printed full bleed. A foreword by Eugenio López Alonso and a preface by Patrick Charpenel open the volume. Larratt-Smith's essay, Psychedelic Antiquity, considers the place of Greek and Roman mythology in Twombly's art. He argues that the works never depict a myth literally, and that myth let Twombly express emotion without disclosing its biographical source. Takaaki Matsumoto designed the book, which Damiani published with Fundación Jumex Arte Contemporáneo.

The selection covers the whole of Twombly's career, from pieces made in the early 1950s to the Camino Real paintings he finished shortly before his death in 2011. López Alonso writes in the book that his interest in Twombly began at almost the same time that he started collecting.
description.artist_bio: Cy Twombly (1928-2011), American painter, sculptor and photographer.
description.exhibition_context: Museo Jumex, Mexico City, June 5 to October 12, 2014; described by the publisher as the first comprehensive Twombly exhibition in Latin America.
